description: The project in dirty/ holds the booking service's code, and two facts in it would change a requirement. schema.sql allows one booking of a room a day, a rule the input does not mention and under which a booking that does not overlap is still refused. purge.py deletes a cancelled booking after 7 days, where the input says 30 days as today. Each gets a question that names its file. The contradicted statement is not written, the other three are, and no requirement comes from the code.

must_match.why: the one-booking-a-day rule limits a response the input asks for, so a question names the file and asks about it
the code deletes after 7 days and the input says 30 as today, so a question names the file and both values

must_match.pattern: ^FR-\d+: When an employee books a room for a time slot, the booking service shall store the booking and return the booking ID\.
must_match.why: a statement a constraint limits is still written, from the input's words
the input names the booking service and the project holds its code, so the skill reads the files

must_not_match.why: the statement the code contradicts is not written until the user answers, and the code's 7 days is never a requirement

must_not_match.pattern: (?i)^(FR|NFR)-\d+[^\n]*\b((same|a|per|each|that|any|one) day|one booking|on a day|for a day)\b
must_not_match.why: the one-booking-a-day rule is in the code only: no requirement is written from it
a name, field, or status code taken from the code is in a requirement
a question about a fact in the code carries no proposal

expectations: One question says that the code allows only one booking of a room on a day, names a file under booking_service/, and asks whether a booking that does not overlap is still refused on such a day.
One question says that the code deletes a cancelled booking after 7 days while the input says 30 days, names a file under booking_service/, and asks which applies.
No requirement states a behaviour, value, or name that appears only in the code and not in the task's input.
manual: Each question that names a file states a fact the file really shows.
No question asks about how the code is built: its table, its field names, its status codes 201 and 204, or its cron job.
The transcript shows at most 5 files of booking_service/ read.
